knowledge_point.title: Sketching the Solution Curves of a Differential Equation

question.:question/problem: Which of the following shows some of the solution curves of the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{3}{x}?$ for $x>0$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Integrating the equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{3}{x})\,\text{d}x \\ y & =3\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3\ln|x|+C \\ y & =3 \ln{\left(x \right)}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now plot the solution curves by selecting different values for $C.$ The sketch below shows the solution curves for $C=-2,0,2.$ for $x>0$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186096698/plots/a439cfb56fb669693ff7aa964ccfcce50dcb39f26b6991353cc007e78480e0a6.png)

question.:question/problem: Which of the following shows some of the solution curves of the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=2 x + 4?$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (2 x + 4)\,\text{d}x \\ y & =2\int x + 2\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\left(\frac{\left(x + 2\right)^{2}}{2}\right)+C \\ y & =\left(x + 2\right)^{2}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Which of the following shows some of the solution curves of the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=- \frac{9 \left(x + 2\right)^{2}}{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Integrating the equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (- \frac{9 \left(x + 2\right)^{2}}{2})\,\text{d}x \\ y & =- \frac{9}{2}\int \left(x + 2\right)^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =- \frac{9}{2}\left(\frac{\left(x + 2\right)^{3}}{3}\right)+C \\ y & =- \frac{3 \left(x + 2\right)^{3}}{2}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now plot the solution curves by selecting different values for $C.$ The sketch below shows the solution curves for $C=-2,0,2.$

question.:question/problem: Which of the following shows some of the solution curves of the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{9 e^{\frac{3 x}{2}}}{4}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Integrating the equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{9 e^{\frac{3 x}{2}}}{4})\,\text{d}x \\ y & =\frac{9}{4}\int e^{\frac{3 x}{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{9}{4}\left(\frac{2 e^{\frac{3 x}{2}}}{3}\right)+C \\ y & =\frac{3 e^{\frac{3 x}{2}}}{2}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now plot the solution curves by selecting different values for $C.$ The sketch below shows the solution curves for $C=-2,0,2.$

question.:question/problem: Which of the following shows some of the solution curves of the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{4 e^{\frac{2 x}{3}}}{9}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Integrating the equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{4 e^{\frac{2 x}{3}}}{9})\,\text{d}x \\ y & =\frac{4}{9}\int e^{\frac{2 x}{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{4}{9}\left(\frac{3 e^{\frac{2 x}{3}}}{2}\right)+C \\ y & =\frac{2 e^{\frac{2 x}{3}}}{3}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now plot the solution curves by selecting different values for $C.$ The sketch below shows the solution curves for $C=-2,0,2.$
